headline: Serve one copy of each crypto primitive instead of two
summary: The browser assets and the server code were separate builds of the same upstream packages, installed and versioned independently. They drifted — a framework refresh moved the server halves and left the browser halves a release behind. The framework now publishes browser builds, so both halves come from it.

items.title: The browser crypto assets come from the vendored framework
items.body: `/js/noble-ciphers.js`, `/js/noble-hashes.js` and `/js/noble-pq.js` were each bundled here from their own npm install, alongside the copy the framework vendors for the server: two builds of one package, resolved separately, versioned separately, and listed separately in the SBOM. That arrangement drifted in the obvious way — the browser halves sat on @noble/ciphers 2.2.0 and @noble/post-quantum 0.6.1 while the server halves had moved to 2.3.0 and 0.7.0. The framework now publishes browser builds of the same primitives, so those three assets are copied from it, and their recorded versions are written from its manifest on every refresh rather than restated here. The exported names, the algorithms and the URLs the pages load are unchanged, and encapsulation, sealing and key derivation were checked against the server halves in both directions. The files are larger, because the framework's builds carry more of each package than this project calls — roughly 50 KB more across the three, uncompressed and cached after first load, against a class of drift that is otherwise only caught by looking for it.

items.title: The vendored framework moves to 0.18.20
items.body: Beyond the browser builds above, a response that had already committed its status line no longer has a second status written over it, and the streaming helper stopped replacing a content type the route had set — a download arrived with the right filename and the wrong type. Neither is reachable here: this server registers its own error handler and none of its routes stream a response in parts.
